evidence.title: Electrical Current Effects on Rolling Contact Fatigue Damage in Bearing Steels: The Role of Inclusions
evidence.abstract: Bearings used in wind turbines and electric vehicles are increasingly exposed to stray electrical currents that accelerate rolling contact fatigue (RCF) and promote premature failure through white etching crack (WEC) formation. Although electrically assisted bearing failures have been extensively investigated, the influence of AISI 52100 steel composition on WEC formation remains poorly understood. This study compares the RCF performance of two commercially produced AISI 52100 bearing steels with similar hardness but different inclusion characteristics using an electrically loaded Micro Pitting Rig under five DC electrical loading conditions and lubricated with a WEC-forming gearbox oil. Bearing steel composition exerted a greater influence on fatigue performance than hardness. Steel 1 consistently exhibited longer RCF life and lower wear than Steel 2 despite its slightly lower hardness and higher overall inclusion content. Fatigue performance was governed primarily by the chemistry and local distribution of non-metallic inclusions, with MnS-containing inclusions identified as the predominant crack initiation sites. Electrical loading generally had a limited effect on fatigue life; however, low anodic current density increased RCF life by approximately fourfold through reduced friction, milder wear, and delayed crack initiation. Subsurface observations revealed two complementary WEC formation mechanisms: progressive near-surface tribomutation and inclusion-assisted crack initiation at the depth of maximum subsurface shear stress. These findings provide mechanistic insight into electrically assisted WEC formation and inform the design of more reliable bearing steels for electrified drivetrains.

evidence.title: Fatigue Crack Growth and Stress‐Based Assessment of a Wind Turbine Main‐Bearing Model Under Simulated and Monitoring‐Based Inputs
evidence.abstract: Wind turbine main‐bearing crack assessment requires consistent treatment of material crack growth and operating‐load uncertainty. Fatigue crack‐growth tests were performed on GCr15 0.5‐T CT specimens at , 0.10, and 0.50, and Paris parameters were identified. Finite element simulation at agreed with experiments within 15%. A laboratory‐scale NU205E surrogate was then used for static contact analyses with prescribed semielliptical raceway cracks. Increasing surface‐crack length caused a nonlinear rise in maximum von Mises stress, whereas increasing crack depth reduced the local maximum because of stress redistribution. A normalized Basquin‐based fatigue‐life index was used only for comparative assessment. The monitoring response–based equivalent input produced higher local stresses than the simulated input, increasing inner‐ and outer‐raceway peaks by 16.7% and 26.4%, respectively. The framework distinguishes local stress response from fracture mechanics–based remaining life.

cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. cemetery_warnings.lesson:

A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Inclusion chemistry and distribution govern crack initiation sites in rolling contact fatigue (RCF) under high slip conditions** (domain knowledge: inclusion-assisted fatigue crack nucleation; evidence: MnS inclusions are predominant crack initiation sites).
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace AISI 52100 steel with a modified composition of **AISI 52100 steel with reduced MnS inclusions and optimized non-metallic inclusion chemistry** (e.g., replacing MnS with TiN or Al₂O₃ via ladle metallurgy and Ca treatment).

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Low anodic electrical current density (≤50 mA/mm²) delays WEC formation via reduced friction and milder wear** (domain knowledge: electrochemical tribology; evidence: low anodic current increases RCF life 4x via friction reduction).
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Integrate **active anodic current suppression** in the planetary bearing circuit via **insulated bearing housing segments** and **low-voltage DC bias (≤50 mA/mm²)** applied to the intermediate-speed shaft during high-slip operation (detected via slip sensors).

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Progressive near-surface tribomutation (microstructural transformation) accelerates WEC formation under high slip** (domain knowledge: tribomutation in bearing steels; evidence: two complementary WEC mechanisms include near-surface tribomutation).
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Apply **surface nitriding (SQ treatment) to a depth of 0.3–0.5 mm** on the raceway of intermediate-speed planet bearings to **stabilize the near-surface microstructure** against tribomutation, combined with **reduced lubricant additive concentration** (phosphorus/sulfur <0.1 wt%) to minimize WEC-promoting chemistry.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The same **inclusion-assisted crack initiation mechanism** (shared with the source system), where non-metallic inclusions (specifically MnS-containing) act as stress concentrators under high slip conditions, initiating white etching cracks (WECs) at the depth of maximum subsurface shear stress. Domain knowledge: Rolling contact fatigue (RCF) in bearings is governed by subsurface shear stress fields (Lundberg-Palmgren theory), and inclusions disrupt material continuity, amplifying local stress.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Modify the intermediate-speed planet bearing steel composition to reduce MnS inclusion density and optimize inclusion morphology (e.g., via calcium treatment or vacuum degassing) while maintaining hardness and mass constraints.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The same **progressive near-surface tribomutation mechanism** (shared with the source system), where repeated sliding under high slip induces microstructural changes (e.g., dislocation cell formation, phase transformations) near the surface, weakening material resistance to crack propagation. Domain knowledge: Tribomutation is a known precursor to WEC formation in bearings under mixed lubrication (Kahraman et al., 2011).
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Apply a **surface-hardened layer** (e.g., nitriding or shot peening) to the planet bearing raceways to a depth of 0.3–0.5 mm, targeting the tribomutation-affected zone while avoiding mass penalties (<0.5% weight increase).

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The same **electrically assisted friction reduction mechanism** (shared with the source system), where low anodic current density (via stray currents or intentional biasing) reduces friction and delays crack initiation by mitigating asperity contact. Domain knowledge: Electrical contact in bearings can alter tribochemical reactions (e.g., reducing oxidative wear) and modify friction via surface charge effects (Godfrey, 1999).
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Integrate a **low-voltage anodic bias system** (5–10 V DC) into the gearbox housing, connected to the planet bearings via insulated current paths, to establish a controlled anodic current density of 0.1–0.5 A/m² during operation.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Domain knowledge (rolling contact fatigue mitigation via inclusion modification) + Evidence (MnS inclusions as crack initiation sites)**. Replace MnS-containing inclusions with oxide-based inclusions (e.g., Al₂O₃) to eliminate the primary crack initiation sites while preserving hardness and bulk material properties. The mechanism preserves the subsurface shear stress distribution but alters the local chemistry to suppress inclusion-assisted crack initiation.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace the AISI 52100 steel composition with a variant containing **Al₂O₃-based inclusions** (≤5 ppm MnS) while maintaining hardness (60–62 HRC) and similar overall inclusion volume fraction. Use calcium treatment to refine inclusion morphology.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Domain knowledge (electrochemical mitigation via anodic protection) + Evidence (low anodic current density increases RCF life 4x via reduced friction)**. Introduce a **sacrificial anodic coating** (e.g., zinc-nickel alloy) on the bearing raceway to locally suppress stray current density at the rolling contact, replicating the effect of low anodic current density without modifying bulk steel composition.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Apply a **5–10 µm thick zinc-nickel anodic coating** to the raceway tracks of the intermediate-speed planet bearings, designed to corrode preferentially under stray current conditions. Coating must maintain **≤0.2 µm Ra surface finish** post-application to avoid tribological penalties.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Domain knowledge (subsurface stress redistribution via geometry) + Evidence (WEC formation at depth of maximum subsurface shear stress)**. Modify the bearing raceway **cross-sectional profile** to shift the location of maximum subsurface shear stress away from the inclusion-rich zone (typically 0.1–0.3 mm below surface) toward a deeper, inclusion-poor region (0.4–0.6 mm).
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace the **standard logarithmic raceway profile** with a **modified "deep-shear" profile** featuring a **concave inflection at 0.4 mm depth**, increasing the effective contact ellipse aspect ratio by 15% while maintaining identical nominal contact stress (calculated via Hertzian analysis). Requires **re-grinding of raceways** with a custom cam profile.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **White etching crack (WEC) initiation under high slip is driven by localized adiabatic heating and microstructural transformation in the bearing material (e.g., martensitic transformation in through-hardened steels), exacerbated by boundary lubrication failure.** Domain knowledge: WEC is a known failure mode in rolling bearings under high slip conditions (e.g., >3% slip ratio), where frictional heat induces phase changes and hydrogen embrittlement. Evidence basis: "white etching crack formation under high slip" and "axial cracking of the intermediate-speed planet bearings."
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: **Replace through-hardened bearing rings with case-hardened (e.g., carburized) rings with a hardened case depth of ≥1.5 mm and a core hardness of ≤35 HRC.** This creates a thermal gradient barrier to suppress adiabatic heating in the raceway and reduces susceptibility to microstructural transformation. Retain the same outer dimensions to maintain crane capacity constraints.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **Axial cracking in intermediate-speed planet bearings is driven by differential thermal expansion between the bearing ring and housing/gear shaft, induced by localized frictional heating under high slip.** Domain knowledge: High slip in planetary gearsets generates asymmetric thermal gradients, causing axial stress concentrations at the bearing ring ends. Evidence basis: "axial cracking" and "high slip" imply a thermomechanical failure mode.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: **Introduce a circumferential thermal barrier coating (e.g., plasma-sprayed aluminum oxide, 0.2–0.5 mm thickness) on the outer raceway of the bearing rings to reduce heat transfer to the housing.** Additionally, implement a **preloaded axial retention system (e.g., tapered roller bearing with axial preload of 5–10% of radial load)** to mitigate axial stress concentrations. Mass impact: Coating adds <100 kg; preload system adds <200 kg (well within 12-tonne limit).

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: **High slip conditions lead to lubricant breakdown and asperity contact, generating micro-welding and debris formation that accelerates WEC propagation via a tribochemical mechanism.** Domain knowledge: WEC in bearings is often linked to lubricant degradation products (e.g., iron oxides, organic residues) that embed in the raceway and act as stress risers. Evidence basis: "white etching crack formation under high slip" implies lubricant failure is a co-factor.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: **Replace mineral oil-based lubricant with a fully formulated polyalphaolefin (PAO)-based grease with extreme-pressure (EP) additives (e.g., sulfurized molybdenum disulfide) and a base oil viscosity of 220 cSt at 40°C.** Additionally, implement a **dual-lubrication system** where the grease is replenished via a centralized lubrication unit every 6 months (automated via nacelle monitoring). Mass impact: Grease system adds <300 kg (tank + pump).

CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.justification: R377 patent-text ground truth (TOSCANINI/R377_PATENT_TEXT_FETCH.json + R377_PATENT_TEXT_GROUND_TRUTH.json): 12/30 family representatives (40%) were substantively irrelevant cross-domain term collisions (CWDM optical link for a battery-thermal candidate; dental-condition monitoring for rolling stock; bone fracture forceps for rail steel...). A hit sharing NO entity term with the candidate now needs >= 3 NON-generic mechanism terms to be mechanism art: the measured true cross-domain analog (line-pipe steel with hydrogen fracture toughness for a rail-steel candidate) shares 3 non-generic terms and survives; every measured false positive shares <= 2 and is demoted. This RAISES the cross-domain bar (was the same >= 2 as same-domain) — stricter, not weaker (Art. VII).
CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap remains a proxy; entity word-sense collisions ('gear': steering vs draft) can still pass — disclosed limitation, not a solved problem

MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.justification: same term-overlap rule family as the pipeline relevance adjudicator and the Q2 instrument (>= 2 shared content terms = domain-specific rather than accidental collision); NOT weakened relative to any prior gate
MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap is a proxy for mechanism identity

ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.justification: a family ANTICIPATES only when nearly ALL elements of the candidate's FULL distinguishing set (uncapped — the claim elements, not the 6-term query core) appear in the family's claim/abstract text; 0.8 leaves a >= 20% element margin — anything lower would convert partial art into a kill (Art. XXVIII forbids). Measured adversarial case: a domain-only patent reached 0.857 against a capped denominator whose true differentiators (acoustic, multi-modal) had been ranked out
ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.uncertainty: claim coverage measured by term overlap, not a claim chart; recorded per family with evidence tier

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: M3_REFINED electrothermal SMA retrieval
informational.lesson: ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages mask catastrophic failure modes. Thermal activation in a 37°C body environment has a narrow window (37-45°C = 8°C max). Sensor electronics are a SPOF that cannot be fully resolved by redundancy (common-mode failures).

informational.mechanism: M5_REFINED adaptive over-drainage controller (sleep-state + venous pressure)
informational.lesson: Do not assume VP shunt problems apply to the eShunt. The eShunt's drainage geometry is fundamentally different (short path, no siphon). Always verify the problem exists for the SPECIFIC device geometry. Over-drainage is siphon-driven; without a hydrostatic column, it may not occur.

informational.mechanism: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

A combination qualifies only if it produces a demonstrably new technical effect that survives prior art and non-obviousness attack. warnings.lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: Bearings used in wind turbines and electric vehicles are increasingly exposed to stray electrical currents that accelerate rolling contact fatigue (RCF) and promote premature failure through white etching crack (WEC) formation. Although electrically assisted bearing failures have been extensively investigated, the influence of AISI 52100 steel composition on WEC formation remains poorly understood. This study compares the RCF performance of two commercially produced AISI 52100 bearing steels with similar hardness but different inclusion characteristics using an electrically loaded Micro Pitting Rig under five DC electrical loading conditions and lubricated with a WEC-forming gearbox oil. Bearing steel composition exerted a greater influence on fatigue performance than hardness. Steel 1 consistently exhibited longer RCF life and lower wear than Steel 2 despite its slightly lower hardness and higher overall inclusion content. Fatigue performance was governed primarily by the chemistry and local distribution of non-metallic inclusions, with MnS-containing inclusions identified as the predominant crack initiation sites. Electrical loading generally had a limited effect on fatigue life; however, low anodic current density increased RCF life by approximately fourfold through reduced friction, milder wear, and delayed crack initiation. Subsurface observations revealed two complementary WEC formation mechanisms: progressive near-surface tribomutation and inclusion-assisted crack initiation at the depth of maximum subsurface shear stress. These findings provide mechanistic insight into electrically assisted WEC formation and inform the design of more reliable bearing steels for electrified drivetrains.

custody_records.raw_content: Wind turbine main‐bearing crack assessment requires consistent treatment of material crack growth and operating‐load uncertainty. Fatigue crack‐growth tests were performed on GCr15 0.5‐T CT specimens at , 0.10, and 0.50, and Paris parameters were identified. Finite element simulation at agreed with experiments within 15%. A laboratory‐scale NU205E surrogate was then used for static contact analyses with prescribed semielliptical raceway cracks. Increasing surface‐crack length caused a nonlinear rise in maximum von Mises stress, whereas increasing crack depth reduced the local maximum because of stress redistribution. A normalized Basquin‐based fatigue‐life index was used only for comparative assessment. The monitoring response–based equivalent input produced higher local stresses than the simulated input, increasing inner‐ and outer‐raceway peaks by 16.7% and 26.4%, respectively. The framework distinguishes local stress response from fracture mechanics–based remaining life.
